A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bayes-adaptive offline reinforcement-learning work. Their complete main text, Appendices A–E, equations, algorithms, figures, and tables are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on twelve D4RL MuJoCo tasks and three simulated tokamak tracking tasks, plus prediction-error analyses, ablations, and runtime measurements in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark, simulation, ablation, prediction-error, and runtime results in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The ensemble belief updates, reward penalties, Continuous BAMCP algorithm, and search-based policy iteration are unchanged. The MOBILE-based penalty variant in Appendix E.4 already appears in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use HalfCheetah, Hopper, and Walker2d with the same four dataset qualities, and the same tokamak electron-temperature, ion-rotation, and beta-n tracking tasks. No training or evaluation scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches throughout Tables 1, 2, 8, and 10, including the model-based and model-free baselines. Sampled EfficientZero and the separately reported CBOP replication also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, rollout procedures, metrics, and evaluation settings match in Section 5 and Appendices C–E. Both retain evaluation without test-time search and the same final-ten-epoch score aggregation.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component comparisons, belief-adaptation prediction analyses and rollout examples, reward-penalty ablation, and computational-cost comparisons. Section 5 and Appendix E contain no added or revised supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain three-run reporting, standard deviations in result tables, and 95% confidence bands in Figures 1, 2, and 4. Table 10 specifies the same random seeds, 0, 1, and 2.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, BA-MCTS averages 74.45 in Table 1 and 80.25 with the MOBILE penalty in Table 10 in both versions. All plotted results also match.

T1.justification: The BAMDP definitions, mathematical equations, root-sampling Lemma A.1 and its proof, and the argument explaining why double progressive widening invalidates root-sampling equivalence are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning Bayesian offline MBRL, continuous stochastic tree search, and policy iteration, together with the same empirical superiority claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of belief adaptation and deep search are retained. So are qualifications concerning finite-action supervised updates, model inaccuracies, hyperparameter sensitivity, and additional offline training cost in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

D1.justification: Implementation choices, hyperparameters, tokamak preprocessing and simulator details, hardware specifications, and training-time disclosures are unchanged. Both provide the same codebase access statement.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to Bayesian offline/meta-RL, BAMCP, PUCT, and MuZero variants are unchanged. Reference entries reflow without adding or removing works.

P1.justification: v3 adds Le Xu to the author list and updates affiliations and the corresponding-author email. The title, scientific prose, section sequence, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page layout and subsequent text and reference breaks change, including moving the Introduction heading to the right column. Algorithm 2's caption and rules become blue. Figures and tables retain their content and organization.

improvement.justification: v3 updates authorship and institutional/contact information and makes minor presentation changes. The methods, theoretical reasoning, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations remain the same, including Appendices A–E. These changes do not materially improve or weaken the paper's scientific support or clarity.
